# F00-T03 renderer comparison

Native Windows and Linux measurements select the owned differential renderer within ADR-003's accepted design. Both candidates work for this ASCII spike; the owned prototype is smaller and has lower measured input-to-echo-write latency.

The private spike pins `@earendil-works/pi-tui@1.5.0` (MIT, upstream `e49b1495045f06643a7cc4c93330fabc2ab37ce4`, declared Node >=22.19) and Bun 1.4.2. Production dependencies are unchanged. Both implementations use the same `Transcript.render(width): string[]` ASCII fixture, 34 ms streaming interval, 120-column viewport, and 100 single-character inputs at 70 ms intervals with Enter every 50 characters. Each mode runs with Escape and Ctrl+C separately, resizing 120 -> 80 -> 120 after submission. Final native binaries run in a temporary directory outside the repository and node_modules.

The metric is raw stdin event receipt to return from the stdout write containing that input's complete echo. It includes pi input buffering and render scheduling, excludes transport before stdin receipt and physical screen paint, and does not count stream-only writes. The probe removes CSI formatting and OSC hyperlink resets, treats cursor/erase operations as line boundaries, and rejects prefix-only matches. Samples stay in arrival order; p95 uses nearest rank. This is not the Phase 9 PTY latency gate.

The file list is refined with one focused `spikes/renderer/pty-harness.py` and `.github/workflows/renderer-spike.yml` to collect native Linux evidence from the Windows development host. The coordinator also approved changing only root `scripts.test` from `bun test test` (a substring filter that accidentally includes the spike) to `bun test ./test` (the explicit directory). This preserves all 27 root tests and runs the 10 spike tests in their own workflow with the private dependency installed. Windows uses installed pywinpty 2.0.15 with ConPTY; Linux uses Python's standard PTY library. No test framework or production feature is added. The harness stores raw PTY bytes as UTF-8 logs, stderr including sample JSON, console/termios snapshots, commands, sizes and SHA-256 digests. It checks terminal mode restoration, final cursor/alternate-screen/paste/keyboard/synchronized-output control sequences, normal exits and injected lifecycle failures.

Mechanical corrections to the plan example: initialize timer state before cleanup can run; use shared ASCII components to keep fixture behavior identical; handle resize explicitly; restore terminal/listener/observer state in `finally`; match pi exit controls with `matchesKey`; keep shared comparison code free of pi imports; handle OSC resets and cursor boundaries in the echo probe. A Windows no-op control showed `rtk run -c`'s cmd shell changes console input mode 503 to 487 before renderer startup, so snapshots are taken inside that initialized launch shell around the actual candidate process. The original mismatch was not attributed to either renderer.

Reproduction from the repository root (PowerShell, no global PATH changes):

```powershell
rtk proxy C:/Users/RYZEN/.local/share/lizzy-agent/toolchains/bun-1.4.2/bun-windows-x64/bun.exe install --cwd spikes/renderer --frozen-lockfile
rtk proxy C:/Users/RYZEN/.local/share/lizzy-agent/toolchains/bun-1.4.2/bun-windows-x64/bun.exe test spikes/renderer/compare.test.ts
rtk proxy python spikes/renderer/pty-harness.py --bun C:/Users/RYZEN/.local/share/lizzy-agent/toolchains/bun-1.4.2/bun-windows-x64/bun.exe --rtk C:/Users/RYZEN/.local/bin/rtk.exe --output C:/Users/RYZEN/.local/share/lizzy-agent/reports/renderer-windows
```

Linux CI installs the private frozen lockfile, runs the focused tests and harness self-check, then runs `python3 spikes/renderer/pty-harness.py --output dist/renderer-linux`. Interactive candidate streams inherit a real PTY; CI invokes installed tools directly. Each backend is bundled with `bun build <backend>-entry.ts --target=bun --outfile <backend>-spike.js` and compiled with the same flags plus `--compile` (native `.exe` suffix on Windows). Neither build uses minification. Exact absolute commands and artifact hashes are in `environment.json`.

The spike intentionally excludes a full editor, themes, Unicode, scrollback, physical display timing, and macOS. Enhanced pi exit-key encodings are covered by unit tests; native runs use legacy character/control bytes, with pi keyboard negotiation recorded in the raw log. Optional clipboard and modifier features outside this workload are not implied by successful ASCII sessions.

## Recorded result and selection

Choose the **owned differential renderer** for the subsequent TUI work within ADR-003's accepted design. All eight OS/backend/mode combinations passed the ASCII workload with both exit controls. The owned prototype had p95 below 0.13 ms in every session, a 6,106-byte JS bundle, and no native assets. Pi's p95 ranged from 12.975200 to 16.027800 ms, with a 212,952-byte JS bundle and an optional Windows native helper absent from the standalone build. Pi worked for this ASCII workload; it is not rejected as Bun-incompatible. The selection favors lower scheduling latency, a smaller dependency surface, and explicit terminal lifecycle ownership. Production editor, Unicode and scrollback work still needs the Phase 9 tests.

These measurements were collected on 2026-11-08:
- Windows: source/build SHA `77c97e95bab4b652435e37c11641c67f534e064f`, Windows-10-10.0.22631-SP0, AMD64, Python 3.11.15, native ConPTY via pywinpty 2.0.15, RTK 0.42.4.
- Linux: source/build SHA `c0fc51b3f38c788fb79672db39f5eac17d426651`, Linux-7.0.0-1019-azure-x86_64-with-glibc2.43, x86_64, Python 3.14.4, native Python PTY on GitHub's ubuntu-latest runner.
- Bun: 1.4.2 on both; viewport 120 columns x 30 rows, resized to 80 x 30 and back. The later SHA changes only the Linux harness fork-descriptor handling; renderer sources and both JS bundle hashes are identical. Subsequent report-only commits do not replace these measurement SHAs.
- Windows negotiated pi modifyOtherKeys after ConPTY's device-attributes response; Linux's raw PTY has no terminal emulator to answer capability queries. Inputs were legacy ASCII/control bytes on both. Kitty/modifyOtherKeys exit encodings are unit-tested, not claimed as native Kitty-emulator runs.

| OS | Backend | Mode | Escape p95 ms | Ctrl+C p95 ms | Samples Esc / Ctrl+C | Unanswered | Input, stream, submit, resize, exit, restore |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| Windows | minimal | source | 0.111200 | 0.122500 | 100 / 100 | 0 / 0 | Pass / Pass |
| Windows | minimal | compiled | 0.123600 | 0.123900 | 100 / 100 | 0 / 0 | Pass / Pass |
| Windows | pi | source | 12.975200 | 14.626200 | 100 / 100 | 0 / 0 | Pass / Pass |
| Windows | pi | compiled | 14.206300 | 16.027800 | 100 / 100 | 0 / 0 | Pass / Pass |
| Linux | minimal | source | 0.047069 | 0.048121 | 100 / 100 | 0 / 0 | Pass / Pass |
| Linux | minimal | compiled | 0.053038 | 0.054810 | 100 / 100 | 0 / 0 | Pass / Pass |
| Linux | pi | source | 13.252852 | 14.178011 | 100 / 100 | 0 / 0 | Pass / Pass |
| Linux | pi | compiled | 14.182003 | 14.208484 | 100 / 100 | 0 / 0 | Pass / Pass |

Each normal session exited 0, observed two submits, streaming ticks, and widths ending in 80 -> 120. All removed their data listeners, restored raw mode, matched native before/after console or termios state, and ended cursor/alternate-screen/paste/keyboard/synchronization modes correctly. Source lifecycle-failure injection also exited 1 with the expected error and restored state for both backends on both OSes; these failure checks are separate from the 100-sample latency sessions.

| Native build | Minimal JS bytes | Pi JS bytes | Minimal executable bytes | Pi executable bytes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Windows x64 | 6106 | 212952 | 86093312 | 86299648 |
| Linux x64 | 6106 | 212952 | 81319392 | 81524192 |

Executable sizes include Bun. Pi adds 206,336 bytes on Windows and 204,800 bytes on Linux before optional assets. Both executables were built and executed independently in temporary directories outside node_modules; compiled success was measured, not inferred from a successful build.

Pi's Windows source reported its native platform helper loaded; standalone compiled sessions reported it unavailable but completed the workload. A separate compiled startup/cleanup check successfully loaded the 8,704-byte `native/win32/prebuilds/win32-x64/win32-platform.node` beside the executable, bringing that distribution to 86,308,352 bytes before license notices. The raw result is under `renderer-helper-check/pi-compiled-escape-failure.result.json`. No latency is claimed for that injected-failure check. Linux's clipboard helper is not needed by this headless TTY workload; GUI clipboard and native modifier functionality were not exercised. The owned renderer requires no extra assets.

## Evidence and validation

- Native Linux workflow: [successful run 42474196621](https://github.com/meryzennn/lizzy-agent/actions/runs/42474196621), [renderer-linux artifact](https://github.com/meryzennn/lizzy-agent/actions/runs/42474196621/artifacts/13614237833), 53,602 compressed bytes. Downloaded copy: `C:/Users/RYZEN/.local/share/lizzy-agent/reports/renderer-linux/`.
- Native Windows logs: `C:/Users/RYZEN/.local/share/lizzy-agent/reports/renderer-windows/`. Each session has `.config.json`, `.pty.log`, `.stderr`, `.terminal.json` and `.result.json`; `environment.json` contains commands, platform, viewport, build sizes and hashes. Windows helper verification is in the sibling `renderer-helper-check/` directory.
- Raw samples from all 16 successful sessions are preserved below, independent of CI artifact retention. The artifact/local logs retain terminal output and mode snapshots. The temporary measurement executables are removed after execution; the separately verified helper executable remains in its report directory.
- Local root `bun run check`: 27/27 tests, typecheck and lint exit 0 (pre-existing sync-issues lint notices remain). Spike `bun test ./spikes/renderer/compare.test.ts`: 10/10 tests, 22 assertions. The focused strict TypeScript invocation and `biome check spikes/renderer` pass. Python harness self-checks cover missing samples, unanswered input, resize/submission/restoration failures, terminal-control cleanup and fork descriptor selection.
- At code SHA `c0fc51b3f38c788fb79672db39f5eac17d426651`, the [root check workflow](https://github.com/meryzennn/lizzy-agent/actions/runs/42474196540) passed Ubuntu/Windows and the [baseline measurement workflow](https://github.com/meryzennn/lizzy-agent/actions/runs/42474196594) passed Ubuntu/Windows/macOS. Existing baseline files were not changed; these jobs collect baseline evidence and are not the future regression gate.
- Red/green evidence: the initial TypeScript test failed on the missing compare module, then targeted echo tests exposed cursor-boundary and pi OSC-reset mismatches before fixes. The first Linux [run 42473660453](https://github.com/meryzennn/lizzy-agent/actions/runs/42473660453) failed before candidate startup because `pty.fork()` returns child descriptor -1; the new self-check reproduced that defect, then passed after using descriptor 0 in the child. No latency from that failed harness run is presented as candidate evidence.
- Boundaries: one controlled 100-sample session per exit/backend/mode/OS, no statistical confidence interval, and no physical terminal paint or macOS renderer claim. Windows and Linux scheduling differ; compare candidates within each host. A minimal raw backend intentionally treats any Escape byte as exit and does not support escape-sequence editing. The production license is unchanged; pi remains a private MIT-licensed spike dependency.
